newsitem.title: USA: MCI to carry talk and data on same line.
newsitem.headline: MCI to carry talk and data on same line.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp said it had developed a system to allow voice and data to share a single telephone line, bringing unified communications one step closer.
The technology, dubbed Vault, would allow a customer to talk to and receive computer data from an MCI service representative simultaneously on a single, conventional telephone line.
"From a customer's perspective, communications will be simplified. The issue of which network a communication travels over will be irrelevant," MCI President Tim Price said on Wednesday.

MCI said the cost of Vault is part of the $100 million a year it is already spending on upgrading its Internet networks. The company plans to earn $2 billion a year in Internet revenues by the end of the century.
"What they are proposing is a technological leap in some regards," said Bryan van Dussen, director of telecommunications research at the Yankee Group research firm.
Vault works by putting phone conversations into "packets" and mixing it with data packets carried on the phone line.
Customers currently need separate lines to communicate over a telephone network and a packet-switched network.

In packet switching, traffic is divided into manageable chunks and labeled for its ultimate destination. It is sent via the most convenient route, while conventional phone calls can only travel a route set in advance.
MCI plans to add products suitable for Vault in areas like faxes, document sharing and video conferencing.
